rule: Hot-path code in either implementation never calls a platform or engine transcendental (Math.log, f64::ln) on a path whose output is compared; both call the owned plain-fdlibm port, and conformance is bit-identity to it.
chose: Own the logarithm on both sides. The TypeScript lessons path calls a plain fdlibm __ieee754_log written in TypeScript (core/fdlibm.ts) instead of Math.log, and the Rust core runs the same algorithm unfused on every target. Conformance means bit-identical to that function, which is the same on every Node and every platform
over: (b) relaxing conformance to rank-equivalence with an epsilon; (c) matching each Node build's Math.log per target (D32, built at ed35650), which ties the test matrix to every Node build that exists
because: CI run 35794294826 and the Docker search showed Math.log's result depends on the Node BUILD (clang on macOS arm64 fuses every site, gcc on Linux arm64 two, x86-64 none), so the TypeScript reference itself is not bit-stable: two users on differently built Nodes rank lessons differently from identical code. There was no single TypeScript answer to match. JavaScript arithmetic never contracts, so a TypeScript fdlibm is bit-stable by the language's semantics, and matching it makes the crosscheck platform-independent.
